approachQuestion.prompt:
Stable Temperature Interval

An array `readings` gives consecutive integer measurements. Return the greatest length of a contiguous interval whose maximum minus minimum is at most tolerance. Return zero for empty input.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; -10^9 ≤ readings[i] ≤ 10^9; 0 ≤ tolerance ≤ 10^9.
• Differences use signed 64-bit arithmetic. Preserve the input order.

Examples:
1. readings = [8,2,4,7], tolerance = 4 → 2.
2. readings = [3,3,3], tolerance = 0 → 3.

Choose one approach.
constraints: Differences use signed 64-bit arithmetic. Preserve the input order.

options.text: Maintain increasing and decreasing deques of indices for the current interval. Remove dominated indices from each back when extending right. While the front values differ too much, advance left and expire indices before left. Track the greatest valid length.
options.feedback: Deque fronts identify the true active minimum and maximum. Removing values cannot increase the range, so repairing left is safe.

options.text: Extend right and repeatedly rescan the active interval for its minimum and maximum, removing from the left until valid. Track the best length.
options.feedback: The validity test and boundary rule are correct, but repeated rescans can be replaced by retained extrema candidates.

options.text: Return the longest interval where every adjacent pair differs by at most tolerance.
options.feedback: For [1,3,5], tolerance=2 every adjacent difference is two, but the full interval range is four; the answer is two.

options.text: Maintain only the smallest and largest values ever seen; never change them when left advances.
options.feedback: Expired extrema must disappear. For [100,1,2,3], tolerance=2 the suffix [1,2,3] is valid despite the earlier 100.

feedback.reason: An incoming value dominates older smaller maxima candidates or larger minima candidates that expire sooner.
details: Use two deques of indices, one with increasing values and one with decreasing values. Pop dominated backs on insertion. Advance left while max-front minus min-front exceeds tolerance, expiring front indices before left. Update best after repair. Implement deque ends without array shifting.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Maintain both active extrema” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and 64-bit arithmetic. Deque push/pop at either end has constant amortized cost; do not implement removal by shifting an array.
Include deque storage. Input and scalar output are excluded; no intervals are copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each index enters and leaves each monotone deque at most once.
details: Each index is inserted once into each deque and removed at most once from each. Thus all back pops and front expirations together are linear, and the deques hold at most n indices. Validity is restored by removing a prefix; an invalid earlier start cannot become valid through later extensions.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Every deque removal consumes an index inserted earlier. Total removals across all endpoints are linear, not n per endpoint.
“O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Deque-end operations require no comparison sort or heap-height repair; each index has one insertion/removal lifetime.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: A monotone input can retain a growing set of unresolved extrema indices, so the two working deques are not constant storage.
